_about.purpose: Hand-labelled set for calibrating retrieval (implementation-plan.md Phase 2.4). Retrieval only -- no generation call, no API cost.
_about.labelled: 2026-10-05, after the reading-order fix that corrected every DGA section heading
_about.relevant: A chunk is relevant if it CONTAINS the guidance that answers the question -- not if it is merely on the same topic. A chunk that mentions sugar is not relevant to 'how much free sugar' unless it states a quantity or a limit.
_about.out_of_corpus: relevant is deliberately empty. These exist to set the floor: the best score any of them reaches is the number the floor has to clear.
_about.caveat: Labels are one person's judgement over a 105-chunk corpus and should be reviewed. Where retrieval and the label disagreed, each case was re-read and the resolution is noted in `label_note`.

questions.label_note: The hardest negative in the set, and the most important. The corpus DID contain this figure until 2026-10-05, in an Irish table whose sex-to-figure pairing PDF extraction destroyed; it is now quarantined. The right behaviour is a not-in-corpus refusal, so this question exists to prove the refusal actually fires rather than the retriever finding some adjacent alcohol text and answering anyway.

questions.label_note: Same reason as q27. This question previously retrieved the destroyed calorie-by-age table at rank 1 (0.676, above the floor), which is exactly the path to a confidently wrong number under a valid-looking citation. It must now refuse.
